result.summary:
Ran the FULL suite via `sh scripts/test_parallel.sh` -- real 16-way parallel (N=16 from nproc), TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP=tp3958030 genuinely exported and shared by all 16 partitions per the script's own design. Combined result: 'combined: 1690 tests, 5 properties, 2 failures (1693/1695 passed)', exit 1.

Failure 1 (partition 1): RequirementStatusInvariantsTest A3 -- ISS-0119 itself (docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml over its roll-rule size ceiling). PRE-EXISTING, structurally unrelated: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` never touches that file or its index -- only test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs, two design docs, test/specs/REQ-055.md, and handoffs/.

Failure 2 (partition 4): the AC1 test itself -- 'AC1 timing ratio 36.11x exceeded multiplier 30x (TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP unset)'. THIS IS A REAL REGRESSION CAUSED BY THIS BRANCH, confirmed by reproduction, not a coincidence of load. Root cause: the branch's own new `describe "ISS-0260 -- ac1_timing_multiplier/0"` block (engine_concurrency_test.exs:366-428) registers a describe-level `on_exit(fn -> System.delete_env("TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP"); ... end)` that runs after every test in that block. System.delete_env/1 is OS-process-global. ExUnit's execution order is seed-randomized suite-wide (async:false only rules out CONCURRENT races within the file, not sequential ordering against other tests scheduled before/after it by the seed). When the seed schedules 'returns 60 when TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP is set' before the real AC1 test in the same partition process, that test's own on_exit deletes the TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP variable test_parallel.sh set for the WHOLE partition's lifetime, so AC1 silently falls back to the 30x default multiplier -- reintroducing exactly the flake ISS-0260 exists to fix.

Reproduced deterministically: `export TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP=tp_repro2; mix test test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs --seed 531662 --no-color --trace` (partition 4's own seed). --trace confirms 'ISS-0260 ... returns 60 when TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP is set' runs immediately before AC1. AC1 happened to finish in 4616.4ms this time (under the 30x threshold by luck) but System.get_env("TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP") was provably nil for it -- same mechanism, same defect, just a faster run. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own step-04b run didn't catch this because it never set TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP externally before invoking mix test, so there was nothing for the on_exit to delete.

AC1 itself did NOT reliably run under the intended 60x parallel multiplier in this real 16-way run -- confirmed to have run (and failed) under the 30x default despite TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP being genuinely set for the whole partition.

issues.description: describe-level on_exit unconditionally calls System.delete_env("TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP"), which is OS-process-global, not per-test. Under real seed-randomized ExUnit ordering this can delete the partition-wide TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP value scripts/test_parallel.sh exports for the whole partition process, before the real AC1 test in the same file/process runs -- causing AC1 to run under the wrong (30x default) multiplier and fail. Reproduced deterministically outside the full suite run (see report yaml).
issues.fix_belongs_in: test code (this branch's own new tests), not application code
issues.suggested_fix: Capture System.get_env("TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP") (and TEST_AC1_TIMING_MULTIPLIER) at setup time, and in on_exit restore exactly that captured value (put_env if it was originally set, delete_env only if it was originally nil) instead of unconditionally delete_env.

result.next_action: Return to TEST-DESIGNER to fix the on_exit teardown bug in the ISS-0260 ac1_timing_multiplier/0 describe block, then back through TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and TEST-RUNNER before this branch can merge. Do NOT route to Step 5 (ISSUE-FIXER close) -- ISS-0260's own fix is not yet verified stable under the real parallel regime it targets.
